coverage.limits: Inspected as XML text: titles, element labels, technology tags, descriptions, relationship labels, data-entity-1/data-entity-2 attributes, arrowhead polygons and bounding coordinates. No visual rendering. Cluster nesting and label-overlap checked arithmetically from x/y/width values only.
Same text-level inspection. No access in this pass to workspace.dsl or the main design document to confirm which labels are explicit versus implied.
Same text-level inspection. Deployment node technology strings taken literally.
Same text-level inspection. This is a subset component view; absence of a component here is only a defect where the view's own title scope or an edge in this view requires it.

findings.evidence: Containers.svg link lnk19 (Android bridge APK -> App-private catalog/configuration) = "Appends ordered bounded events and cleanup state"; Deployment.svg lnk8 carries the identical label. ExecutionComponents.svg lnk21 (CallbackBroker -> App-private catalog/configuration) has the identical label, while lnk24 (CatalogRepository -> App-private catalog/configuration) = "Owns transactional writes and read-only snapshots" has no container-level counterpart. Containers.svg lnk17 (APK -> Android OS and target apps) = "Uses supported version/module/interface/reachability probes" is identical to ExecutionComponents lnk17 (DeviceViewResolver -> OS), while ExecutionComponents lnk18 (InvocationPlanner -> OS) = "Performs authorized SDK/Binder/paired ADB operation" has no container-level counterpart.
findings.issue: The container and deployment views describe the APK's relationship to its SQLite store as only callback-journal appends and its relationship to the OS as only probes. The APK's authorized SDK/Binder/paired-ADB invocations and its catalog/policy/view/audit persistence are invisible at container level. The verbatim label reuse indicates the container edges are the first-declared component edge propagated (Structurizr implied-relationship behaviour) rather than deliberate container-level summaries. A reader of the container view would conclude the APK never invokes OS operations.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Declare explicit container-level relationships with summary descriptions in the model: APK -> SQLite "Reads catalog snapshots, policy/grants, groups, resolved views; writes overlays, journal, audit (transactional)"; APK -> Android OS and target apps "Probes version/module/interface/reachability; performs authorized SDK/Binder/paired-ADB invocations"; keep the separate OS -> APK callback edge. Re-export Containers and Deployment.
findings.verification_needed: workspace.dsl pass: confirm whether container-level relationships are declared or only implied, and the !impliedRelationships setting.

findings.evidence: Deployment.svg lnk9: "Offline catalog tooling" (in Build workstation) -> "Android bridge APK" (in Android phone / One app UID and process) labelled "Supplies validated versioned catalog release" with no technology tag. Containers.svg lnk16 identical, no technology tag.
findings.issue: A runtime deployment edge crosses from a workstation node to a phone process with no channel, format, integrity check or trigger. It is unspecified whether the catalog release is a build-time bundled asset, an owner-initiated import through the Compose UI, or a file transfer, and who verifies the version/hash before the immutable import required by Requirement 5. As drawn the edge is not implementable.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Tag the relationship with the delivery mechanism and integrity contract (for example "versioned catalog bundle with manifest hash; bundled at build time and/or imported by the local owner through the management UI; verified before immutable import"). If delivery is build-time only, replace the runtime deployment edge with a build-time note on the Build workstation node.
findings.verification_needed: Main design document catalog import section; workspace.dsl relationship technology.

findings.evidence: Deployment nodes present: "Android phone [Deployment Node: Android35+]" containing "One app UID and process [Deployment Node: Kotlin Android APK]", and "Build workstation [Deployment Node: Existing local toolchain]". No node for an MCP client host, an ARC controller host, or the phone's adbd; no ADB link or port-forward relationship; the external software systems from the Container view (MCP client, Compatible ARC client, Compatible external ARC target, Android OS and target apps) are absent. Subtitle: "Reference deployment; not installed by this task".
findings.issue: Requirement 3 specifies same-device paired ADB and remote-host loopback forwarding, and the Container view tags the ARC edge "[arc-protobuf-v1 loopback TCP]". Loopback-bound listeners reached through ADB forwarding, and the paired same-device ADB path to adbd, are deployment-topology decisions with security consequences, and the deployment view is the only view where they can be shown. The reference deployment models neither.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Add a "Remote agent host" deployment node (software system instances: MCP client, Compatible ARC client, ADB client) and an infrastructure node "adbd (wireless debugging, paired)" inside the Android phone node. Add relationships: remote host -> phone "ADB forward of the MCP and ARC loopback ports"; APK -> adbd "paired same-device ADB over loopback". Keep the honest "not installed by this task" subtitle.
findings.verification_needed: Main design document deployment and ADB sections for the intended topology wording.

findings.evidence: lnk22: CallbackBroker -> McpServer "Signals URI-only resource update and bounded reads". McpServer description: "Pinned MCP2025-11-25 transport, sessions and bounded resource reads". McpServer has no outgoing edge to CallbackBroker, CatalogRepository or App-private catalog/configuration in this view.
findings.issue: A resources/read of journal pages is a pull initiated by McpServer, but the only edge mentioning reads is a push from CallbackBroker. The component that serves bounded journal pages, and the store it reads from, is not modeled. If the static model has no McpServer -> CallbackBroker (or -> repository) relationship, a dynamic callback view cannot legitimately show the read step either.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Split into two edges: CallbackBroker -> McpServer "Signals resources/updated (URI only)" and McpServer -> CallbackBroker "Reads bounded journal pages by application cursor (resources/read)"; if the repository serves the journal instead, point the read edge at CatalogRepository.
findings.verification_needed: CallbackFlow.svg and workspace.dsl (other passes): confirm which component serves resources/read and that a static read relationship exists.

findings.evidence: InvocationFlow steps: "3: Submit exact schema and scope plan", "4: Pin compatible binding and coherent types", "5: Recheck current document and contract pins", "6: Admit once, no replay of uncertain effects", "7: Invoke permitted backend", "8: Record bounded outcome". AdmissionGate description: "Canonical policy, approvals, epochs and dispatch boundary". ExecutionComponents: AdmissionGate outgoing edges only to DeviceViewResolver, CatalogRepository and InvocationPlanner; no edge to App-private catalog/configuration or any policy store.
findings.issue: The view titled "Authenticated invocation and canonical admission" contains no step that evaluates the per-client MCP grant, the owner approval or the current epoch, and no view in this pass shows where approvals and epochs are persisted or read. Requirement 5 makes the per-client grant a distinct authority from declared metadata and OS authority; the canonical-admission flow omits exactly that check.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Insert a step between 3 and 4: "AdmissionGate -> policy store (SQLite via CatalogRepository or a dedicated component): evaluate per-client grant, owner approval and expected epoch; on failure return a structured denial that is also audited". Add the matching static relationship so the dynamic view is valid.
findings.verification_needed: ServerCoreComponents.svg / ServerComponents.svg / main document: if a policy store and this step exist there, this remains a view-completeness defect; if absent everywhere, escalate to high.

findings.evidence: GroupFlow steps: "1: Discover groups for a job and context budget" (MCP client -> McpServer), "2: Authenticate request", "3: Search summaries only", "4: Read full searchable index and dependency closure", "5: Report permission status; no grant change", "6: CAS activate chosen coherent set or return conflict" (McpServer -> FunctionalGroupIndex). No DeviceViewResolver in the view; no second client request; no result or tools list_changed step. ExecutionComponents lnk13 assigns "Checks selected availability and type closure" to AdmissionGate -> DeviceViewResolver.
findings.issue: The flow titled "atomic interest activation" activates a "chosen coherent set" through FunctionalGroupIndex alone, while the static view places availability and type-closure checking under AdmissionGate and DeviceViewResolver. The two views disagree on who establishes coherence at activation. Step 6 also has no client trigger ("chosen" implies a second request), no returned epoch or conflict, and no mention of the best-effort tools/list_changed notification that Requirement 9 says cannot guarantee host context.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Add "1b: MCP client -> McpServer: Activate selected group set with expected epoch"; add "6a: FunctionalGroupIndex -> AdmissionGate -> DeviceViewResolver: verify availability and type closure for the whole set before CAS commit"; add "7: McpServer -> MCP client: new epoch or conflict; emit notifications/tools/list_changed (best effort, no host-context guarantee)".
findings.verification_needed: Main document group activation section and workspace.dsl dynamic view definition.

findings.evidence: lnk14 data-entity-1="...FunctionalGroupIndex" data-entity-2="...AdmissionGate", label "5: Report permission status; no grant change"; arrowhead at AdmissionGate.
findings.issue: The index needs grant status from the policy owner to annotate ranked summaries (Requirement 8: summaries carry grant status). As drawn the index reports status to the gate, which inverts the information flow or mislabels a query.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Relabel: "5: Query per-client grant status for summaries (read-only; discovery cannot change grants)".

findings.evidence: ExecutionComponents lnk12 McpServer -> AdmissionGate: "Submits exact admitted operation plan". InvocationFlow step 3 on the same pair: "Submit exact schema and scope plan".
findings.issue: A plan submitted to the admission gate is not yet admitted; the static label is circular and contradicts the dynamic label for the same edge.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Relabel the static edge "Submits exact schema and scope plan for admission".

findings.evidence: "Android phone [Deployment Node: Android35+]".
findings.issue: There is no Android version 35; API level 35 corresponds to Android 15. The label conflates version name and API level. A deployment floor is legitimate, but Requirement 6 forbids API-level-only reasoning for bindings, so the floor must be stated precisely and must match the minSdk in the main document.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: "[Deployment Node: Android 15+ (API level 35, app minSdk 35)]".
findings.verification_needed: Main document: confirm the stated minSdk.

findings.evidence: APK description: "One UID and initially one process; Kotlin service owns authoritative state". Deployment node name: "One app UID and process".
findings.issue: "initially" hedges toward an unspecified future multi-process split, while the deployment node and Requirement 2 commit to one coherent process. The condition and consequences of a split (for the unexported local facade and SQLite ownership) are undefined.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Delete "initially", or append "(single process; any later service-process split must keep the unexported local facade and SQLite ownership in the service process)".

findings.evidence: SQLite container description: "Catalog snapshots, policy, groups, views, event journal and audit". GroupFlow/InvocationFlow: "ClientAuthenticator [Component: Kotlin / Keystore]" with "Credential, principal and session ownership".
findings.issue: Requirement 2 places client mapping, permissions and configurable logging in SQLite. The container description omits client mapping and logging configuration, and the views do not say where the client-to-principal mapping lives relative to Keystore-held secrets.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Description: "Catalog snapshots, overlays, policy/grants, client mapping, logging configuration, groups, resolved views, event journal and audit; secrets held in Android Keystore".

findings.evidence: "Offline catalog tooling [Container: Python / Gradle docs]" with description "Source acquisition/extraction/schema validation and reference fixtures; no phone operations".
findings.issue: The technology tag merges the documentation build (Requirement 11 Gradle tasks for the design deliverable) with the catalog extraction tooling. The description covers only catalog work. Not a catalog-correctness judgement; it is a container identity defect.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Tag "[Container: Python]"; if the documentation toolchain is intentionally modeled, make it a separate container or deployment-node note outside the runtime software system.

findings.evidence: MCP edge technology: "[Authenticated MCP]" only. ARC client -> APK: "[arc-protobuf-v1 loopback TCP]". APK -> Compatible external ARC target: no technology tag. Android OS -> APK "Calls verified callback endpoint; authority remains separate": no technology tag. Local owner -> APK: no technology tag.
findings.issue: Transport and binding decisions required by Requirements 3 and 9 (pinned MCP 2025-11-25 transport, loopback binding, authentication mechanism) are absent from the MCP edge, and the two ARC edges are tagged inconsistently although both carry the same wire protocol.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: MCP edge: "[MCP 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP, loopback bind, bearer/session]" (or the transport actually specified in the main document); both ARC edges: "[arc-protobuf-v1 raw TCP, signed 4-byte big-endian length, loopback/forwarded]"; callback edge: "[Binder/AIDL callback or SDK listener]"; owner edge: "[Compose UI, in-process]".
findings.verification_needed: Main document transport section for the exact MCP transport wording.

findings.evidence: ARC client description: "Existing arc-protobuf-v1 remote-control client". APK -> external target: "Connects and validates exact retained ARC profile".
findings.issue: "arc-protobuf-v1" is a third identifier alongside the required envelope protocol version 1.0 and package 0.8.0, and its definition is not visible in these views. "validates exact retained ARC profile" can be read as a dedicated handshake, which Requirement 4 says the protocol does not have; validation can only occur on the first request/response envelope.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Define "arc-protobuf-v1" once (retained profile = envelope protocol version 1.0, package 0.8.0, pinned commit 19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919) and relabel the edge "Connects; validates envelope version on the first response (no separate handshake)".
findings.verification_needed: ArcComponents.svg, main document ARC section, remote_control.proto.

findings.evidence: lnk16 DeviceViewResolver -> CatalogRepository: "Streams full inventory and persists atomic resolved view".
findings.issue: On an edge directed from resolver to repository, "Streams full inventory" reads as the resolver supplying inventory to the repository; the inventory is read from the repository. One label mixes a pull and a push.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: "Reads full inventory stream; persists resolved device view atomically (CAS)".

findings.evidence: InvocationPlanner description: "Typed generic/raw dispatch, codecs, Binder and ADB adapters"; lnk18 "Performs authorized SDK/Binder/paired ADB operation"; no separate ADB component in the view.
findings.issue: Requirement 2 asks for separate MCP/ADB/device-view health, Requirement 3 for paired ADB with forwarding, and Requirement 4 for a separate ADB backend behind ARC. The invocation view internalizes ADB as an adapter inside the planner, leaving pairing state, health and sharing with ARC unplaced.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: If an ADB backend component exists elsewhere in the model, show InvocationPlanner -> that component "Executes paired ADB commands for uninstrumented targets" and remove "ADB adapters" from the planner description; if none exists, add one.

findings.evidence: Last steps: "7: Invoke permitted backend" (InvocationPlanner -> Android OS) and "8: Record bounded outcome" (AdmissionGate -> AuditLogger). No McpServer -> MCP client response step; no denial branch.
findings.issue: Under call/return semantics AdmissionGate can own the outcome, but the view never states that, never shows the final JSON-RPC result reaching the client with SSE termination (Requirement 9), and shows no denied path for a view whose subject is admission.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Add "9: McpServer -> MCP client: final JSON-RPC result or structured error; POST SSE stream terminates" and a note "denial at 4, 5 or 6 returns a structured error and is audited at 8".

findings.evidence: Each file's <title> contains unrendered markup, for example "<size:24>Container View: Android MCP bridge</size>".
findings.issue: Creole sizing markup leaks into SVG metadata; accessible titles and link previews will show the raw tags.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Strip size markup from the diagram title in the export, or post-process the <title> element in the Gradle SVG task.

findings.evidence: "One app UID and process [Deployment Node: Kotlin Android APK]" contains "Android bridge APK [Container: Kotlin / Jetpack Compose]".
findings.issue: A node whose technology is the APK containing a container that is the APK is tautological and hides the actual runtime unit (an app sandbox process under one uid).
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Node: "App sandbox process [Deployment Node: Android app process, single uid]".

findings.evidence: Bridge description: "Complete binding inventory with separate authority and contextual discovery"; Versioned public sources: "unknown coverage retained".
findings.issue: "Complete" is a strong claim next to a source box that retains unknown coverage; the mechanism claim is retention of the full inventory including unknown/unreachable entries with reasons.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: "Full retained inventory including unknown/unreachable entries with reasons; separate authority; contextual discovery".

limitations: No tools were used; all observations come from reading the SVG XML text supplied in this message.
Relationship direction was taken from data-entity-1/data-entity-2 attributes and arrowhead positions; label meaning was inferred from the literal strings.
The implied-relationship explanation in P3-F01 is an inference from identical label strings and Structurizr's documented default behaviour, not a confirmed reading of workspace.dsl.
Visual rendering, font fallback and reader-facing layout were not inspected; overlap checks are arithmetic only.
